## Root cause

`anndata.experimental.concat_on_disk` with `join="outer"` reindexes the alternate axis (varm values, via `_write_alt_mapping`) on **on-disk arrays returned by `read_as_backed`** — h5py/zarr dense datasets and backed sparse datasets. `Reindexer.apply` in `source/src/anndata/_core/merge.py` had no branch for either type:

- h5py `Dataset` fell into `_apply_to_array` → `pd.api.extensions.take` → `AttributeError: 'Dataset' object has no attribute 'take'`.
- Backed sparse (`BaseCompressedSparseDataset`) likewise hit pandas and was treated as a 0-d scalar → `IndexError: tuple index out of range`.

## Fix (12 lines, only `source/src/anndata/_core/merge.py`)

Added two dispatch branches to `Reindexer.apply`, following the class's existing pattern (DataFrame/sparse/awkward/dask/cupy each materialize differently):

- `H5Array | ZarrArray` → materialize with the already-imported `asarray()` (registers `x[...]` for h5py, `np.asarray` for zarr), then `_apply_to_array`.
- `BaseCompressedSparseDataset` → `el.to_memory()`, then `_apply_to_sparse`.

This repairs the shared primitive, so every caller (alt-axis mappings, layer/X paths) benefits, and reindexing stays on-demand: arrays are only materialized when a reindex is actually applied.

- Public workbench passes; result is `6 obs × 8 var`, `varm/projection_basis` correctly reindexed to the outer var index.
